column4: This is CALENDAR., Eiden Group's internal scheduling system. One workspace for meeting rooms in Casablanca and Agadir, training formations, the clients who rent from us, and everything the team needs to stay on the same page. This short video walks through the whole thing, from signing in to the admin settings. Architecture for Time — that's the product promise, and you'll feel it from the first screen.

Staff accounts are created for you by an admin — there is no public sign-up and no password guessing. You sign in with your Eiden Group email and password. Enter something wrong and the app simply says the email or password is incorrect, without revealing which one it was. Forgot your password? The link on this screen sends a single-use reset to your inbox, valid for one hour.

The moment you sign in, you land on a live dashboard. Today's bookings at the top, the week ahead of you, the next three events, room utilization for the week, formation fill rates, and anything waiting on you right now — a pending change request will sit here until you handle it. Everything is pulled from the live database; nothing on this screen is decorative.

The top strip is your week, Monday to Saturday at Eiden Group. Tap any day to jump straight to it in the calendar. Below the numbers, your week's room grid shows what's booked where — the busiest room, the quietest room, all at a glance.

The calendar is the heart of the product. Four views: Week, Day, Month, and Agenda. Week and Day render the time grid you book on; Month shows occupancy at a distance; Agenda is the next fourteen days as a flat, printable list. Weekend columns are shaded and the current time is marked with a line, so you never lose your place in the day.

To create a booking, drag across empty cells on the grid — the drawer opens with those exact times filled in. Or hit New booking at the top right, or press N anywhere in the app. Fill in the title, pick the room, the client, the category, the rate — save, or send.

Here's the rule the product is built around. Two bookings want the same room at the same time? The app tells you immediately, shows you the conflict, and offers free slots nearby — right there in the drawer. You pick one and move on. Never an accidental double-booking.

If neither side can move, you can send a change request to the person who already holds the slot. They get an email, they approve or decline with one click, or it expires after seventy-two hours. You see the status of every request under Requests. The room is never double-booked while the question is being answered.

Plans are Eiden Group's internal roadmap for training operations — quarterly goals, launches, and long arcs. They're not Jira; they're intentionally simple. Drag cards between columns, drop tasks onto a plan, and mark them done as you go.

Formations, or training sessions, are full-fidelity bookings: capacity, waitlist, attendance, and a participant roster you can paste in directly from a CSV export — or type in one by one. Every formation carries its seat count against the room it runs in.

Clients keeps the people behind the phones. Company accounts and individuals, their booking history, contact information, preferences — and for anything private, an anonymize-on-demand that redacts name, email, phone, address, tags and notes while preserving the aggregates you still need for reporting. GDPR-clean without losing the numbers.

Reports shows you the business: utilization by room, revenue by category, formation performance against capacity — all filtered by Casablanca or Agadir, or all locations. One click downloads any panel as CSV. If you pay an accountant, they'll like it too.

The Inbox tab is a live view of the Eiden Group mailbox, read-mail only — no delete, no archive, no moving. Messages arrive here within seconds. Read them, reply, mark as read, attach files the other way around — the conversation stays in one place. It's wired directly to the Hostinger mailbox over IMAP, with the same server credentials the rest of the app uses.

Every meaningful thing — a change request landing, a slot being approved or declined, an expiry, a new welcome — generates a notification with a link straight to the request. The bell turns blue and waits for you. Nothing fires twice, and nothing fires if you've turned it off in Settings.

This is Requests. Open requests, where each one sits in the negotiation between whoever holds the slot and whoever needs it. Approve to move it, decline with a note, or cancel your own request if you've found another time. Every outcome is logged, and the other side is emailed automatically.
Admins run the house from Settings. Everything below is live the moment you press save — no deploy, no republish. Rooms, categories, team, working hours — let's walk through them.

Rooms are what the whole product orbits. Name, location — Casablanca or Agadir — capacity, hourly rate, notes, amenities. Toggle one off and it vanishes from the booking pickers for everyone, immediately. Rates are snapshotted onto each booking at creation time, so past invoices never change when you raise a price.

Categories tag every booking for reporting: Meeting Room Rental, Formation, Event, and yours. Each carries an English and a French name, a tint color, an icon, and a sort order. System categories can be renamed but never deleted — they anchor every report.

Team is the only place staff accounts exist. Create one and the person gets an email with a one-time password valid until their first login. Roles are Admin or Staff: staff can't deactivate colleagues, can't touch working hours or business settings, and can't remove rooms. You control all of it here.

Working hours per weekday, exactly the ones the booking engine respects. Closed days are off the grid entirely. Pick a slot increment — fifteen minutes, thirty, sixty — and a buffer between bookings for turnover. The whole app follows this, not just the calendar.

General is the business identity: name, legal form, logo — upload and it's live everywhere they render — public site URL, phone, city, currency. This is what goes on invoices and in the footer of every email the system sends.

Every transactional email has a switch: booking created, updated, cancelled, formation reminders, change requests, the welcome note with the one-time password. Turn any of them off and the system silently stops sending it — you won't be bothered, and neither will they.

The product speaks French and English everywhere — the toggle in the top-right corner flips the entire interface for you, remembered next time you visit. Date formats, 24-hour cycles, week starts on Monday, amounts in MAD with narrow no-break spaces — all of it follows the locale you pick.

The audit log is the whole story: every write, every actor, every timestamp. Filter by action, export as CSV — invaluable the day something looks wrong, and a small price to pay for the peace of mind that everything is traceable.

Every environment has a Mail tab that pings the real mailbox: IMAP handshake, SMTP send, and a one-click test email to your own address. If the connection breaks, this page tells you before your clients do.

Data and privacy is the honesty drawer. Export the entire workspace as one JSON snapshot — bookings, clients, rooms, plans, settings — or anonymize a client on request: name, phone, email, address, tags, notes, all redacted, while the aggregates you still need for the books stay put. Irreversible, on purpose, with a typed confirmation.

Every screen answers to the keyboard. Command-K opens the palette — pages, actions, search, EN and FR toggle, sign out — fuzzy-filtered as you type. Press ? at any time for the full cheatsheet. N starts a booking anywhere, G then D jumps to the dashboard, G then I to the inbox, and left and right arrows flip the calendar period. Left hand never leaves the keys.

Switch to French and every word, date, format and email changes with it. This is the same product — not a translation overlay — and the whole team at Eiden Group uses both, usually without noticing which they're in.

If you forget your password, the reset link lands in your inbox, good for one hour. If the whole team is locked out because the mailbox creds rotated, the admin panel reaches the same mailbox with the same credentials — and the log shows you why every send failed.

That's the tour: sign in, the live dashboard, a calendar that refuses to double-book, formations and clients, reports, mail, an admin panel that's honest about everything it does — and the same product in English and French, every screen, every email. CALENDAR. — Architecture for Time. Open it at calendar dot eiden dash group dot com, or ask your admin for the link. See you in the schedule.
